ai.description: Toenayar novemcarinata reaches 10 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a pale lateral stripe and nine distinct dorsal keels. A dark mid-lateral band runs from the snout through the eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Toenayar novemcarinata* is best distinguished by the presence of exactly nine distinct longitudinal keels on its dorsal scales, a feature lacking in other Indian mabuyas.
ai.habitat: *Toenayar novemcarinata* inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations up to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Anderson's Mabuya is a diurnal skink that primarily forages for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky outcrops during the sunlit hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Toenayar novemcarinata* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Toenayar novemcarinata* is found in the Western Ghats of India, primarily across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka, at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,200 meters.
